topic: software supply chain; code review effectiveness; evidence validation
status: bounded research lead; file-position effect itself is not novel
claim: Controlled evidence already shows a defect-class-specific code-review position effect, while a 2026 large field study finds a small later-position association using a noncausal post-review bug-fix proxy. The actionable gap is to test transportability across defect classes and real PR contexts, while validating default file order/comments against actual inspection and independently adjudicated defects.
positive_evidence: Fregnan et al. analyze 219,476 PRs and run a controlled study with 106 participants; one of two seeded defect types has 64% lower detection odds when last rather than first, while the other has no position effect.

The 2026 study mines 330,343 multi-file merged PRs/756,814 file instances from 182 repositories; later position has higher proxy-label rates (56.7% at position 1 to 61.5% at position 30), but associations are small (r=.022, rho=.018, Cramer's V=.062).

The 2026 authors explicitly state that their file-level proxy does not establish defect introduction or review causality, and that path order/comments do not exactly capture actual inspection/semantic review.
counterevidence: The 2022 controlled study finds no position effect for one of its two defect types, limiting blanket claims.
The 2026 field paper's proxy outcome may include older defects, later requirements, or maintenance, and file complexity/churn/coupling are incompletely controlled.
Prior evidence shows file position and comment activity have already been studied; a broad novelty claim is rejected.

sources.title: First Come First Served: The Impact of File Position on Code Review
sources.sections: abstract; field study and controlled seeded-defect result

sources.title: Does Order Matter? An Empirical Investigation into the Impact of File Ordering on Code Review Effectiveness

falsifiable_test: In consenting repositories, randomize or step-roll out file ordering, instrument actual files viewed/time, and pre-register defect-detection sensitivity by defect type, complexity, coupling, churn, PR size, and reviewer experience. Link field results to later fixes only after independent adjudication; do not label every later bugfix as missed review. The lead weakens if no reproducible class-specific position effect remains after randomized exposure or if comments/default position closely track actual inspection and detection.
limitations: One newly audited observational paper plus one targeted prior controlled study; not a systematic review. The 2022 experiment and 2026 field proxy are not commensurate outcomes; this is a triangulation design lead, not a direct effect-size comparison.

topic: software supply chain security; adoption and outcome validation
status: bounded cross-paper research lead; not evidence of tool ineffectiveness or global novelty
claim: Signing usability/adoption, developer-reported issue taxonomies, CI configuration hardening, anomaly scores, and autonomous-mitigation claims occupy distinct evidence stages. The cell motivates prospective studies that connect intervention adoption to verified artifact integrity, exploitability/reachability, remediation latency, and incidents while retaining denominators and deployment context.
positive_evidence: The 17-practitioner Sigstore interview study identifies integration, privacy, enterprise, and offline-workflow barriers but measures no breach reduction.
The AI supply-chain paper's 753-post thematic sample builds a taxonomy from developer reports; it is not an incident-prevalence sample, and its 100-record keyword-free classifier test is limited.

The GitHub Actions study observes configuration changes rather than prevented incidents; the autonomous-defense paper reports >90% mitigation and <6% overhead but lacks detail for independent reproduction in the reviewed text.
counterevidence: Identity signing and tighter workflow permissions can provide meaningful provenance and least-privilege controls even if this cell does not estimate incident reduction.
The autonomous-defense paper does report strong simulated/deployment claims; inadequate audit detail limits independent confidence but does not falsify them.
The developer taxonomy is useful for discovering concrete classes of reported issues and mitigation needs, even without prevalence inference.

falsifiable_test: Follow repositories before/after verifiable signing or automated remediation adoption; measure signed-artifact coverage, identity/key failures, confirmed malicious or vulnerable artifact reachability, remediation latency, and incidents per release/deployment. Use matched or randomized rollout, pre-register threat model, preserve denominators, and publish artifacts. The lead weakens if adoption/configuration metrics robustly predict independently confirmed outcomes across ecosystems and deployment contexts.
limitations: Single six-version cell with three new reads, heterogeneous adjacent evidence, and targeted rather than systematic follow-up. Does not estimate effectiveness or imply controls do not work.
